source: Sanskrit and transliteration: gita/gita open dataset (public domain). English meanings and notes written for Thinker's Log.

1.title: Arjuna's despair
1.summary: Two armies of one family face each other at Kurukshetra. Arjuna asks Krishna to drive his chariot between them, sees teachers, cousins and friends on the other side, and collapses. The whole Gita is the answer to this moment: what to do when duty and feeling pull in opposite directions.
1.reflect: Where in your work or life are you facing a choice where every option costs someone you care about?

verses.sa:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच
धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः।
मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय॥
verses.tr:
dhṛitarāśhtra uvācha
dharma-kṣhetre kuru-kṣhetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ
māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāśhchaiva kimakurvata sañjaya
verses.en: Dhritarashtra said: Sanjaya, on the field of dharma, at Kurukshetra, my sons and the sons of Pandu gathered, eager to fight. What did they do?
verses.note: The Gita opens with a blind king asking for news he cannot see for himself. Kurukshetra is called a field of dharma: the battlefield is also a place where right and wrong get tested. Read it as any decisive arena where your values meet reality.

verses.sa:
अर्जुन उवाच
कृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत्।
दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम्॥
verses.tr:
arjuna uvācha
dṛiṣhṭvemaṁ sva-janaṁ kṛiṣhṇa yuyutsuṁ samupasthitam
verses.en: Arjuna said: Krishna, seeing my own people standing here eager to fight, I am overcome with pity and sinking in sorrow.
verses.note: Arjuna's crisis begins with seeing faces, not armies. Abstractions are easy to fight; people are not. This is the moment every leader meets when a decision stops being a slide and becomes the names of real people.

verses.sa:
गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते।
न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः॥
verses.tr:
gāṇḍīvaṁ sraṁsate hastāt tvak chaiva paridahyate
na cha śhaknomy avasthātuṁ bhramatīva cha me manaḥ
verses.en: My bow Gandiva slips from my hand, my skin burns, I cannot stand steady, and my mind seems to whirl.
verses.note: The greatest archer of his age cannot hold his bow. The Gita takes the body's response to inner conflict seriously: confusion shows up as physical paralysis before it becomes a thought.

verses.sa:
सञ्जय उवाच
एवमुक्त्वाऽर्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत्।
विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः॥
verses.tr:
sañjaya uvācha
evam uktvārjunaḥ saṅkhye rathopastha upāviśhat
visṛijya sa-śharaṁ chāpaṁ śhoka-saṁvigna-mānasaḥ
verses.en: Sanjaya said: Having spoken this on the battlefield, Arjuna cast aside his bow and arrows and sank down on the seat of the chariot, his mind overwhelmed with grief.
verses.note: The chapter ends with withdrawal. Arjuna's arguments for not fighting sound noble, but they come from grief, not clarity. Krishna's teaching starts by separating the two.

2.title: The steady mind (Sankhya yoga)
2.summary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with two ideas. First, the self is not the body: what is real in us is not born and does not die. Second, act fully but without clinging to results. The chapter ends with a portrait of the sthitaprajna, the person of steady wisdom. Many readers treat this chapter as the whole Gita in miniature.
2.reflect: Which result are you clinging to so tightly that it is making your action worse?

verses.sa:
कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावः पृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः।
यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मे शिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम्॥
verses.tr:
kārpaṇya-doṣhopahata-svabhāvaḥ
pṛichchhāmi tvāṁ dharma-sammūḍha-chetāḥ
yach-chhreyaḥ syānniśhchitaṁ brūhi tanme
śhiṣhyaste ’haṁ śhādhi māṁ tvāṁ prapannam
verses.en: My nature is overcome by weakness, and my mind is confused about what is right. I ask you: tell me for certain what is best for me. I am your student; I have come to you for refuge. Teach me.
verses.note: Learning begins when Arjuna admits he does not know. Until this verse he argues; here he asks. A first-principles mind starts the same way, by naming the confusion honestly instead of defending a position.

verses.sa:
श्री भगवानुवाच
अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे।
गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः॥
verses.tr:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
aśhochyān-anvaśhochas-tvaṁ prajñā-vādānśh cha bhāṣhase
gatāsūn-agatāsūnśh-cha nānuśhochanti paṇḍitāḥ
verses.en: The Lord said: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, yet you speak words that sound wise. The wise grieve neither for the living nor for the dead.
verses.note: Krishna's first move is gently ironic: Arjuna's reasons sound wise but come from sorrow. The test of wisdom is not how good an argument sounds but whether it comes from a clear mind.

verses.sa:
देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा।
तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति॥
verses.tr:
dehino ’smin yathā dehe kaumāraṁ yauvanaṁ jarā
tathā dehāntara-prāptir dhīras tatra na muhyati
verses.en: Just as the embodied self passes through childhood, youth and old age in this body, so it passes into another body. The steady are not confused by this.
verses.note: You have already been a child, a student and a young professional, and you were 'you' through all of it. The verse asks what that continuous 'you' really is, beneath the changing roles and bodies.

verses.sa:
न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचि न्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः।
अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे॥
verses.tr:
na jāyate mriyate vā kadāchin
nāyaṁ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ
ajo nityaḥ śhāśhvato ’yaṁ purāṇo
na hanyate hanyamāne śharīre
verses.en: The self is never born and never dies. It did not come into being and will not cease to be. Unborn, eternal, everlasting and ancient, it is not killed when the body is killed.
verses.note: This is the metaphysical root of the Gita: what you most deeply are cannot be destroyed. Whether you take it literally or as a stance, it removes fear as the driver of action.

verses.sa:
वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि।
तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णा न्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही॥
verses.tr:
vāsānsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya
navāni gṛihṇāti naro ’parāṇi
tathā śharīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇānya
nyāni sanyāti navāni dehī
verses.en: As a person discards worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, the embodied self discards worn-out bodies and enters new ones.
verses.note: One of the Gita's most famous images. It frames death as a change of clothes, not an end. Practically, it invites holding forms lightly: bodies, roles, titles, and identities you will one day take off.

verses.sa:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि॥
verses.tr:
karmaṇy-evādhikāras te mā phaleṣhu kadāchana
mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo ’stvakarmaṇi
verses.en: You have a right to your actions alone, never to their fruits. Do not let the fruits of action be your motive, and do not be attached to inaction.
verses.note: The most quoted verse of the Gita. Do the work fully; let go of owning the outcome. Note the second half: this is not permission to stop. Detachment from results is meant to make action better, not smaller.

verses.sa:
योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते॥
verses.tr:
yoga-sthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā dhanañjaya
siddhy-asiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṁ yoga uchyate
verses.en: Established in yoga, perform your actions, Arjuna, giving up attachment, the same in success and failure. This evenness of mind is called yoga.
verses.note: Here yoga is defined not as posture but as samatvam, evenness. A decision-maker who is the same in success and failure sees the situation instead of their own hopes and fears.

verses.sa:
दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः।
वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते॥
verses.tr:
duḥkheṣhv-anudvigna-manāḥ sukheṣhu vigata-spṛihaḥ
vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhaḥ sthita-dhīr munir uchyate
verses.en: One whose mind is not shaken in sorrow, who does not crave pleasures, and who is free from attachment, fear and anger, is called a sage of steady wisdom.
verses.note: The portrait of the sthitaprajna. Notice the list: attachment, fear and anger. These are exactly the forces that distort judgement in a crisis.

verses.sa:
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते।
सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते॥
verses.tr:
dhyāyato viṣhayān puṁsaḥ saṅgas teṣhūpajāyate
saṅgāt sañjāyate kāmaḥ kāmāt krodho ’bhijāyate
verses.en: When a person dwells on objects of the senses, attachment to them arises. From attachment comes desire, and from desire comes anger.
verses.note: A precise causal chain, almost a systems diagram: attention, then attachment, then desire, then anger when the desire is blocked. The leverage point is the first link, where your attention goes.

verses.sa:
क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः।
स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति॥
verses.tr:
krodhād bhavati sammohaḥ sammohāt smṛiti-vibhramaḥ
smṛiti-bhranśhād buddhi-nāśho buddhi-nāśhāt praṇaśhyati
verses.en: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, confusion of memory; from confused memory, the loss of judgement; and with the loss of judgement, one is ruined.
verses.note: The chain continues to collapse. Anger clouds perception, which corrupts memory, which destroys judgement. Compare it with Kahneman: emotion first, then the story that justifies it.

3.title: Selfless action (Karma yoga)
3.summary: Arjuna asks: if knowledge is higher than action, why fight? Krishna answers that no one can avoid acting, so the question is how to act. Work done as an offering, without selfish attachment, frees instead of binds. Leaders matter most, because others copy what they do.
3.reflect: What do the people around you copy from you, whether you intend it or not?

verses.sa:
न हि कश्चित्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत्।
कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः॥
verses.tr:
na hi kaśhchit kṣhaṇam api jātu tiṣhṭhatyakarma-kṛit
kāryate hyavaśhaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛiti-jair guṇaiḥ
verses.en: No one can remain without action even for a moment. Everyone is driven to act, helplessly, by the qualities born of nature.
verses.note: Inaction is not an option; even withdrawing is a choice with consequences. So the real question is never whether to act but in what spirit.

verses.sa:
नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः।
शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः॥
verses.tr:
niyataṁ kuru karma tvaṁ karma jyāyo hyakarmaṇaḥ
śharīra-yātrāpi cha te na prasiddhyed akarmaṇaḥ
verses.en: Do your prescribed duty, for action is better than inaction. Even the maintenance of your body would not be possible without action.
verses.note: A plain, practical verse. The Gita does not glorify escape. Doing your proper work well is itself the spiritual path.

verses.sa:
तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर।
असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः॥
verses.tr:
tasmād asaktaḥ satataṁ kāryaṁ karma samāchara
asakto hyācharan karma param āpnoti pūruṣhaḥ
verses.en: So, without attachment, always do the work that has to be done. By working without attachment, a person reaches the highest.
verses.note: Duty plus non-attachment is the formula. The work is not lessened; only the anxious grip on the result is.

verses.sa:
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः।
स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते॥
verses.tr:
yad yad ācharati śhreṣhṭhas tat tad evetaro janaḥ
sa yat pramāṇaṁ kurute lokas tad anuvartate
verses.en: Whatever a great person does, others follow. Whatever standard they set, the world follows it.
verses.note: The Gita's leadership verse. Culture is set by what leaders do, not what they say. It applies directly to anyone who leads a team.

verses.sa:
प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः।
अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते॥
verses.tr:
prakṛiteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśhaḥ
ahankāra-vimūḍhātmā kartāham iti manyate
verses.en: All actions are performed by the qualities of nature. But one deluded by ego thinks, 'I am the doer.'
verses.note: Outcomes come from countless causes: people, conditions, timing. Seeing this is humbling and also freeing. It is close to systems thinking: structure, not the individual ego, produces most results.

verses.sa:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्।
स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः॥
verses.tr:
śhreyān swa-dharmo viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt sv-anuṣhṭhitāt
swa-dharme nidhanaṁ śhreyaḥ para-dharmo bhayāvahaḥ
verses.en: Better your own duty done imperfectly than another's duty done well. Better to die in your own duty; another's duty is full of danger.
verses.note: Svadharma: your own nature and calling. Imitating someone else's path, however impressive, is risky. Find the work that is genuinely yours.

verses.sa:
श्री भगवानुवाच
काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः।
महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम्॥
verses.tr:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
kāma eṣha krodha eṣha rajo-guṇa-samudbhavaḥ
mahāśhano mahā-pāpmā viddhyenam iha vairiṇam
verses.en: The Lord said: It is desire, it is anger, born of the quality of rajas, all-devouring and most sinful. Know this to be the enemy here.
verses.note: Arjuna asks what drives people to act wrongly against their will. The answer is desire that turns into anger. The enemy is internal before it is external.

4.title: Knowledge and action
4.summary: Krishna reveals that this teaching is ancient and that he appears in every age when dharma declines. He explains the subtle relation between action and inaction, and praises knowledge as the great purifier, gained through humility, questions and service to those who have seen the truth.
4.reflect: Who do you learn from with humility, real questions and service, as 4.34 describes?

verses.sa:
यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत।
अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदाऽऽत्मानं सृजाम्यहम्॥
verses.tr:
yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata
abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānaṁ sṛijāmyaham
verses.en: Whenever dharma declines and adharma rises, Arjuna, I manifest myself.
verses.note: A promise that order is restored whenever it collapses. Read it historically as hope, or personally: in a collapse, something in you rises to set things right.

verses.sa:
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम्।
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे॥
verses.tr:
paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṁ vināśhāya cha duṣhkṛitām
dharma-sansthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge
verses.en: To protect the good, to destroy wrongdoing and to re-establish dharma, I come into being age after age.
verses.note: The purpose of the divine in action: protect, correct, re-establish. Notice it is cyclical, not once and for all. Every generation has to renew its own order.

verses.sa:
कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः।
स बुद्धिमान् मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत्॥
verses.tr:
karmaṇyakarma yaḥ paśhyed akarmaṇi cha karma yaḥ
sa buddhimān manuṣhyeṣhu sa yuktaḥ kṛitsna-karma-kṛit
verses.en: One who sees inaction in action and action in inaction is wise among people; they are a yogi even while performing all actions.
verses.note: A deliberate paradox. A calm mind can be very active without being driven, and doing nothing can be a heavy action with consequences. Look past appearances to what is really happening.

verses.sa:
तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया।
उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः॥
verses.tr:
tad viddhi praṇipātena paripraśhnena sevayā
upadekṣhyanti te jñānaṁ jñāninas tattva-darśhinaḥ
verses.en: Learn this by humble reverence, by sincere questioning and by service. The wise who have seen the truth will teach you this knowledge.
verses.note: Three conditions for real learning: humility, questions and service. Questions are explicitly part of the method; the Gita invites inquiry, not blind belief.

verses.sa:
न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते।
तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति॥
verses.tr:
na hi jñānena sadṛiśhaṁ pavitramiha vidyate
tatsvayaṁ yogasansiddhaḥ kālenātmani vindati
verses.en: In this world there is nothing as purifying as knowledge. One who is perfected in yoga finds it within themselves in due time.
verses.note: Knowledge here means direct understanding, not information. 'In due time' matters: insight ripens with practice; it cannot be forced.

verses.sa:
श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः।
ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति॥
verses.tr:
śhraddhāvān labhate jñānaṁ tat-paraḥ sanyatendriyaḥ
jñānaṁ labdhvā parāṁ śhāntim achireṇādhigachchhati
verses.en: One who has faith, who is devoted to it and who has mastered the senses gains this knowledge, and having gained it, soon reaches supreme peace.
verses.note: Faith, commitment and self-mastery as preconditions for wisdom. Shraddha here means trust strong enough to keep practising before you see results.

5.title: Renunciation of action
5.summary: Is it better to renounce action or to act selflessly? Krishna says both lead to the goal, but selfless action is easier and safer. The wise act without being stained, like a lotus leaf in water, and see the same reality in every being.
5.reflect: Where could you act fully this week while staying untouched, like the lotus leaf?

verses.sa:
ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः।
लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा॥
verses.tr:
brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ
lipyate na sa pāpena padma-patram ivāmbhasā
verses.en: One who acts, offering actions to Brahman and giving up attachment, is not touched by sin, as a lotus leaf is not wetted by water.
verses.note: The lotus leaf sits in water without getting wet. The image says you do not need to leave the world to be free of it; you need a different relation to it.

verses.sa:
विद्याविनयसंपन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि।
शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः॥
verses.tr:
vidyā-vinaya-sampanne brāhmaṇe gavi hastini
śhuni chaiva śhva-pāke cha paṇḍitāḥ sama-darśhinaḥ
verses.en: The wise see with an equal eye a learned and humble Brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog and an outcaste.
verses.note: A radical verse for its time: real wisdom sees the same essence across every social and species boundary. It challenges caste and status hierarchies directly.

verses.sa:
ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते।
आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः॥
verses.tr:
ye hi sansparśha-jā bhogā duḥkha-yonaya eva te
ādyantavantaḥ kaunteya na teṣhu ramate budhaḥ
verses.en: Pleasures born of contact with the senses are sources of sorrow, for they have a beginning and an end, Arjuna. The wise do not delight in them.
verses.note: Anything that begins also ends, so pleasures that depend on circumstances carry their own loss inside them. This is not anti-joy; it points to a joy that does not depend on contact.

verses.sa:
भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम्।
सुहृदं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति॥
verses.tr:
bhoktāraṁ yajña-tapasāṁ sarva-loka-maheśhvaram
suhṛidaṁ sarva-bhūtānāṁ jñātvā māṁ śhāntim ṛichchhati
verses.en: Knowing me as the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, the great lord of all worlds and the friend of all beings, one attains peace.
verses.note: The chapter closes with the divine as suhrdam sarva-bhutanam, the friend of all beings. Peace comes from seeing reality as fundamentally friendly.

6.title: Meditation (Dhyana yoga)
6.summary: Krishna teaches the practice of meditation: how to sit, how to steady the mind, and how to live with balance. The mind is restless, he admits, but it can be trained through practice and detachment. You are your own friend and your own enemy.
6.reflect: In which area is your own mind currently acting as your enemy rather than your friend?

verses.sa:
उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत्।
आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः॥
verses.tr:
uddhared ātmanātmānaṁ nātmānam avasādayet
ātmaiva hyātmano bandhur ātmaiva ripur ātmanaḥ
verses.en: Lift yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. The self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
verses.note: Self-reliance in its deepest form: no one else can raise you. The same mind that drags you down can lift you up.

verses.sa:
बन्धुरात्माऽऽत्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः।
अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत्॥
verses.tr:
bandhur ātmātmanas tasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ
anātmanas tu śhatrutve vartetātmaiva śhatru-vat
verses.en: For one who has mastered the self by the self, the self is a friend. But for one who has not, the self behaves like an enemy.
verses.note: Self-mastery decides whether your own mind works for you or against you. It is a practical test you can run on any bad habit.

verses.sa:
युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु।
युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा॥
verses.tr:
yuktāhāra-vihārasya yukta-cheṣhṭasya karmasu
yukta-svapnāvabodhasya yogo bhavati duḥkha-hā
verses.en: Yoga destroys sorrow for one who is moderate in eating and recreation, balanced in work, and regular in sleep and waking.
verses.note: The Gita's verse on balance: food, rest, work and sleep. Extremes, even spiritual ones, do not work. It reads like modern advice on sustainable performance.

verses.sa:
यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम्।
ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत्॥
verses.tr:
yato yato niśhcharati manaśh chañchalam asthiram
tatas tato niyamyaitad ātmanyeva vaśhaṁ nayet
verses.en: Wherever the restless, unsteady mind wanders, draw it back from there and bring it under the control of the self.
verses.note: This is the whole method of meditation in one line. Wandering is expected; the practice is the return, again and again.

verses.sa:
श्री भगवानुवाच
असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं।
अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते॥
verses.tr:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
asanśhayaṁ mahā-bāho mano durnigrahaṁ chalam
abhyāsena tu kaunteya vairāgyeṇa cha gṛihyate
verses.en: The Lord said: Without doubt, Arjuna, the mind is restless and hard to control. But it can be held through practice and detachment.
verses.note: Krishna agrees with Arjuna that the mind is hard to control. Then he gives two tools: abhyasa (repeated practice) and vairagya (letting go). Neither works alone.

7.title: Knowledge and wisdom
7.summary: Krishna describes his lower and higher natures, the material world and the life principle, and says everything is strung on him like pearls on a thread. Few people seek the truth, and they come for different reasons.
7.reflect: Which of the four reasons in 7.16 brings you to this reading: distress, curiosity, ambition or wisdom?

verses.sa:
मनुष्याणां सहस्रेषु कश्चिद्यतति सिद्धये।
यततामपि सिद्धानां कश्चिन्मां वेत्ति तत्त्वतः॥
verses.tr:
manuṣhyāṇāṁ sahasreṣhu kaśhchid yatati siddhaye
yatatām api siddhānāṁ kaśhchin māṁ vetti tattvataḥ
verses.en: Among thousands of people, hardly one strives for perfection; and among those who strive and succeed, hardly one knows me in truth.
verses.note: Depth is rare. The verse does not discourage; it honours the effort. Most people never start the search; starting already sets you apart.

verses.sa:
मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय।
मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव॥
verses.tr:
mattaḥ parataraṁ nānyat kiñchid asti dhanañjaya
mayi sarvam idaṁ protaṁ sūtre maṇi-gaṇā iva
verses.en: There is nothing higher than me, Arjuna. Everything is strung on me like pearls on a thread.
verses.note: The pearls are visible; the thread is not. The image points to the unseen unity running through diverse things, a pattern a systems thinker will recognise.

verses.sa:
चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन।
आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ॥
verses.tr:
chatur-vidhā bhajante māṁ janāḥ sukṛitino ’rjuna
ārto jijñāsur arthārthī jñānī cha bharatarṣhabha
verses.en: Four kinds of virtuous people worship me, Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise.
verses.note: A non-judgemental list of why people turn to the spiritual: trouble, curiosity, need, or wisdom. Every entry point is valid; what matters is that one enters.

verses.sa:
बहूनां जन्मनामन्ते ज्ञानवान्मां प्रपद्यते।
वासुदेवः सर्वमिति स महात्मा सुदुर्लभः॥
verses.tr:
bahūnāṁ janmanām ante jñānavān māṁ prapadyate
vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti sa mahātmā su-durlabhaḥ
verses.en: After many births, the wise person surrenders to me, knowing that Vasudeva is everything. Such a great soul is very rare.
verses.note: The culmination of wisdom is seeing the divine in everything. 'After many births' signals that this vision is the fruit of long maturing, not a quick insight.

8.title: The imperishable
8.summary: Arjuna asks about Brahman, karma and the moment of death. Krishna teaches that what we dwell on through life shapes where we go at its end, so remember the highest at all times, and keep acting.
8.reflect: What do you dwell on most often? Is it what you would want to be thinking at the end?

verses.sa:
अन्तकाले च मामेव स्मरन्मुक्त्वा कलेवरम्।
यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः॥
verses.tr:
anta-kāle cha mām eva smaran muktvā kalevaram
yaḥ prayāti sa mad-bhāvaṁ yāti nāstyatra sanśhayaḥ
verses.en: Whoever leaves the body at the time of death remembering me alone attains my being. Of this there is no doubt.
verses.note: The last thought matters, but the next verses show it is not a trick: the last thought is the one you have practised all your life.

verses.sa:
तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च।
मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयम्॥
verses.tr:
tasmāt sarveṣhu kāleṣhu mām anusmara yudhya cha
mayyarpita-mano-buddhir mām evaiṣhyasyasanśhayam
verses.en: So remember me at all times, and fight. With your mind and intellect fixed on me, you will surely come to me.
verses.note: The key phrase is 'and fight': remember the highest and keep doing your work. Spirituality and duty run together, not in sequence.

verses.sa:
मामुपेत्य पुनर्जन्म दुःखालयमशाश्वतम्।
नाप्नुवन्ति महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः॥
verses.tr:
mām upetya punar janma duḥkhālayam aśhāśhvatam
nāpnuvanti mahātmānaḥ sansiddhiṁ paramāṁ gatāḥ
verses.en: Having reached me, the great souls do not return to rebirth, this temporary home of sorrow; they have attained the highest perfection.
verses.note: The world is called a temporary home of sorrow. It is a candid view: impermanence is built into everything here, so lasting peace must lie beyond it.

9.title: The royal secret
9.summary: Krishna calls this the king of knowledge and the royal secret: the divine pervades everything yet is not limited by it. Devotion is open to everyone, and the smallest offering made with love is accepted.
9.reflect: What ordinary action this week could you do as an offering, as 9.27 suggests?

verses.sa:
अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते।
तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम्॥
verses.tr:
ananyāśh chintayanto māṁ ye janāḥ paryupāsate
teṣhāṁ nityābhiyuktānāṁ yoga-kṣhemaṁ vahāmyaham
verses.en: Those who worship me with undivided attention, thinking of nothing else, who are always united with me: I carry what they lack and preserve what they have.
verses.note: Yoga-kshema: gaining what you need and keeping what you have. The promise is to those who are wholehearted. Undivided focus is rewarded in spiritual life as in any craft.

verses.sa:
पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति।
तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः॥
verses.tr:
patraṁ puṣhpaṁ phalaṁ toyaṁ yo me bhaktyā prayachchhati
tadahaṁ bhaktyupahṛitam aśhnāmi prayatātmanaḥ
verses.en: Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, that offering of love from a pure heart I accept.
verses.note: The value of an offering lies in the intention, not its size. It democratises devotion: no one is too poor to give a leaf.

verses.sa:
यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत्।
यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम्॥
verses.tr:
yat karoṣhi yad aśhnāsi yaj juhoṣhi dadāsi yat
yat tapasyasi kaunteya tat kuruṣhva mad-arpaṇam
verses.en: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer, whatever you give, whatever discipline you practise, Arjuna, do it as an offering to me.
verses.note: Turn every activity into an offering. This removes the line between sacred and ordinary: a meeting, a meal or a code review can all be done in this spirit.

verses.sa:
समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः।
ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम्॥
verses.tr:
samo ’haṁ sarva-bhūteṣhu na me dveṣhyo ’sti na priyaḥ
ye bhajanti tu māṁ bhaktyā mayi te teṣhu chāpyaham
verses.en: I am the same to all beings; no one is hateful or dear to me. But those who worship me with devotion are in me, and I am in them.
verses.note: The divine plays no favourites, yet a relationship forms through devotion. It is like sunlight, equal to all, but felt most by those who turn towards it.

10.title: Divine manifestations
10.summary: Krishna lists his special manifestations: the best of every kind of thing. The point is not the list but the method: wherever you find excellence, glory or power, see a spark of the divine.
10.reflect: Where have you recently seen excellence that moved you? What was it a spark of?

verses.sa:
अहं सर्वस्य प्रभवो मत्तः सर्वं प्रवर्तते।
इति मत्वा भजन्ते मां बुधा भावसमन्विताः॥
verses.tr:
ahaṁ sarvasya prabhavo mattaḥ sarvaṁ pravartate
iti matvā bhajante māṁ budhā bhāva-samanvitāḥ
verses.en: I am the source of everything; everything comes from me. Knowing this, the wise worship me with deep feeling.
verses.note: The root cause behind all causes. Philosophically it asks the first-principles question taken to its limit: what is the source of everything?

verses.sa:
अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः।
अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च॥
verses.tr:
aham ātmā guḍākeśha sarva-bhūtāśhaya-sthitaḥ
aham ādiśh cha madhyaṁ cha bhūtānām anta eva cha
verses.en: I am the self, Arjuna, seated in the heart of all beings. I am the beginning, the middle and the end of all beings.
verses.note: Before the long list of glories, Krishna gives the essential one: the self within everyone. Look inward first, then outward.

verses.sa:
यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा।
तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसंभवम्॥
verses.tr:
yad yad vibhūtimat sattvaṁ śhrīmad ūrjitam eva vā
tat tad evāvagachchha tvaṁ mama tejo ’nśha-sambhavam
verses.en: Whatever is glorious, beautiful or mighty, know that it springs from a spark of my splendour.
verses.note: A practical way of seeing: treat every excellence you meet, a great engine design, a piece of music, an act of courage, as a glimpse of something larger than its maker.

11.title: The cosmic form
11.summary: Arjuna asks to see Krishna's universal form and is shown it: overwhelming, radiant, devouring time itself. Terrified, he sees that the outcome of the war is already decided; his task is to be the instrument. He then asks to see Krishna's gentle human form again.
11.reflect: Where would it help to see yourself as an instrument of something larger, rather than its sole author?

verses.sa:
दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता।
यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः॥
verses.tr:
divi sūrya-sahasrasya bhaved yugapad utthitā
yadi bhāḥ sadṛiśhī sā syād bhāsas tasya mahātmanaḥ
verses.en: If the light of a thousand suns were to blaze forth all at once in the sky, that might resemble the splendour of that great being.
verses.note: An image of overwhelming light. It points to a reality so vast that ordinary perception breaks down before it.

verses.sa:
श्री भगवानुवाच
कालोऽस्मि लोकक्षयकृत्प्रवृद्धो लोकान्समाहर्तुमिह प्रवृत्तः।
ऋतेऽपि त्वां न भविष्यन्ति सर्वे येऽवस्थिताः प्रत्यनीकेषु योधाः॥
verses.tr:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
kālo ’smi loka-kṣhaya-kṛit pravṛiddho
lokān samāhartum iha pravṛittaḥ
ṛite ’pi tvāṁ na bhaviṣhyanti sarve
ye ’vasthitāḥ pratyanīkeṣhu yodhāḥ
verses.en: The Lord said: I am Time, the great destroyer of worlds, now come forth to annihilate these people. Even without you, all these warriors arrayed against you will cease to exist.
verses.note: Kala, time, is shown as the ultimate force; everything passes. Oppenheimer recalled this verse after the first atomic test. Arjuna's role does not create the outcome, so his fear of being the cause loses its grip.

verses.sa:
तस्मात्त्वमुत्तिष्ठ यशो लभस्व जित्वा शत्रून् भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यं समृद्धम्।
मयैवैते निहताः पूर्वमेव निमित्तमात्रं भव सव्यसाचिन्॥
verses.tr:
tasmāt tvam uttiṣhṭha yaśho labhasva
jitvā śhatrūn bhuṅkṣhva rājyaṁ samṛiddham
mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvam eva
nimitta-mātraṁ bhava savya-sāchin
verses.en: So stand up and win glory. Conquer your enemies and enjoy a prosperous kingdom. They have already been slain by me; be merely the instrument, Arjuna.
verses.note: Nimitta-matram: be only the instrument. Do your part fully while recognising that larger forces decide the result. It releases both arrogance and paralysis.

verses.sa:
मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो मद्भक्तः सङ्गवर्जितः।
निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव॥
verses.tr:
mat-karma-kṛin mat-paramo mad-bhaktaḥ saṅga-varjitaḥ
nirvairaḥ sarva-bhūteṣhu yaḥ sa mām eti pāṇḍava
verses.en: One who works for me, who makes me the goal, who is devoted to me, free from attachment and without enmity towards any being, comes to me, Arjuna.
verses.note: The chapter ends not in spectacle but in conduct: work, purpose, devotion, non-attachment and no hatred. After the vision comes the everyday practice.

12.title: Devotion (Bhakti yoga)
12.summary: Arjuna asks whether to worship the formless or a personal God. Krishna says both reach him, but devotion to a personal form is easier for embodied beings. Then he describes the qualities of a true devotee, one of the Gita's most loved passages.
12.reflect: Which one quality from 12.13 to 12.19 would most change how you lead?

verses.sa:
अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च।
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी॥
verses.tr:
adveṣhṭā sarva-bhūtānāṁ maitraḥ karuṇa eva cha
nirmamo nirahankāraḥ sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ kṣhamī
verses.en: One who bears no ill will to any being, who is friendly and compassionate, free from possessiveness and ego, balanced in pain and pleasure, and forgiving...
verses.note: The portrait begins with relationships: no ill will, friendship, compassion. Spiritual depth shows first in how you treat people.

verses.sa:
यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः।
हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः॥
verses.tr:
yasmān nodvijate loko lokān nodvijate cha yaḥ
harṣhāmarṣha-bhayodvegair mukto yaḥ sa cha me priyaḥ
verses.en: One by whom the world is not disturbed and who is not disturbed by the world, who is free from elation, impatience, fear and anxiety, is dear to me.
verses.note: A two-way peace: you do not agitate others, and others do not agitate you. A useful test for anyone in a high-pressure role.

verses.sa:
समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः।
शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः॥
verses.tr:
samaḥ śhatrau cha mitre cha tathā mānāpamānayoḥ
śhītoṣhṇa-sukha-duḥkheṣhu samaḥ saṅga-vivarjitaḥ
verses.en: One who is the same to enemy and friend, in honour and dishonour, in cold and heat, in pleasure and pain, and free from attachment...
verses.note: Evenness across opposites again, now applied to people and reputation. Praise and blame are weather; they pass.

verses.sa:
तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येनकेनचित्।
अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्तिमान्मे प्रियो नरः॥
verses.tr:
tulya-nindā-stutir maunī santuṣhṭo yena kenachit
aniketaḥ sthira-matir bhaktimān me priyo naraḥ
verses.en: Who is the same in blame and praise, quiet, content with whatever comes, without attachment to a home, steady in mind and full of devotion: that person is dear to me.
verses.note: Contentment with whatever comes is not passivity; it is freedom from needing the world to be a certain way before you can be at peace.

13.title: The field and its knower
13.summary: Krishna distinguishes the field, the body and the whole material world, from the knower of the field, the conscious self. He lists the qualities that make up real knowledge and says that true seeing is seeing the same imperishable reality in all.
13.reflect: Which of the qualities in 13.8 to 13.9 do you most need to cultivate now?

verses.sa:
अमानित्वमदम्भित्वमहिंसा क्षान्तिरार्जवम्।
आचार्योपासनं शौचं स्थैर्यमात्मविनिग्रहः॥
verses.tr:
amānitvam adambhitvam ahinsā kṣhāntir ārjavam
āchāryopāsanaṁ śhauchaṁ sthairyam ātma-vinigrahaḥ
verses.en: Humility, freedom from pretension, non-violence, patience, straightforwardness, service to the teacher, purity, steadiness and self-control...
verses.note: Knowledge, the Gita says, is a set of qualities, not facts. It is a striking definition: you know as much as your character allows you to see.

verses.sa:
इन्द्रियार्थेषु वैराग्यमनहङ्कार एव च।
जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखदोषानुदर्शनम्॥
verses.tr:
indriyārtheṣhu vairāgyam anahankāra eva cha
janma-mṛityu-jarā-vyādhi-duḥkha-doṣhānudarśhanam
verses.en: Detachment from objects of the senses, absence of ego, and keeping in view the pain and evil of birth, death, old age and illness...
verses.note: Seeing clearly includes facing the hard facts of life: ageing, illness and death. Wisdom does not look away from them.

verses.sa:
समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम्।
विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति॥
verses.tr:
samaṁ sarveṣhu bhūteṣhu tiṣhṭhantaṁ parameśhvaram
vinaśhyatsv avinaśhyantaṁ yaḥ paśhyati sa paśhyati
verses.en: One who sees the supreme Lord dwelling equally in all beings, the imperishable within the perishable, truly sees.
verses.note: Ya pashyati sa pashyati: one who sees this, truly sees. Real perception goes beyond surfaces to what is constant beneath change.

verses.sa:
प्रकृत्यैव च कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्वशः।
यः पश्यति तथाऽऽत्मानमकर्तारं स पश्यति॥
verses.tr:
prakṛityaiva cha karmāṇi kriyamāṇāni sarvaśhaḥ
yaḥ paśhyati tathātmānam akartāraṁ sa paśhyati
verses.en: One who sees that all actions are performed by nature alone, and that the self is not the doer, truly sees.
verses.note: Echoing 3.27: actions arise from nature and conditions. The self witnesses. This dissolves much ego, guilt and pride.

14.title: The three gunas
14.summary: All of nature is woven from three qualities: sattva (clarity and harmony), rajas (passion and activity) and tamas (inertia and darkness). They bind the self in different ways. One who rises above all three remains steady whatever arises.
14.reflect: Which guna dominates your week: clarity, restless activity or inertia?

verses.sa:
सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणाः प्रकृतिसंभवाः।
निबध्नन्ति महाबाहो देहे देहिनमव्ययम्॥
verses.tr:
sattvaṁ rajas tama iti guṇāḥ prakṛiti-sambhavāḥ
nibadhnanti mahā-bāho dehe dehinam avyayam
verses.en: Sattva, rajas and tamas, the qualities born of nature, bind the imperishable self to the body, Arjuna.
verses.note: A three-part model of behaviour and mood. It is a useful lens on yourself, teams and even organisations: clear, driven or stuck.

verses.sa:
श्री भगवानुवाच
प्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव।
न द्वेष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति॥
verses.tr:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
prakāśhaṁ cha pravṛittiṁ cha moham eva cha pāṇḍava
na dveṣhṭi sampravṛittāni na nivṛittāni kāṅkṣhati
verses.en: The Lord said: One who does not resent clarity, activity or delusion when they arise, nor long for them when they cease...
verses.note: The one who has risen above the gunas does not fight their moods. They let states arise and pass, like weather, without being ruled by them.

verses.sa:
समदुःखसुखः स्वस्थः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः।
तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः॥
verses.tr:
sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ sva-sthaḥ sama-loṣhṭāśhma-kāñchanaḥ
tulya-priyāpriyo dhīras tulya-nindātma-sanstutiḥ
verses.en: Who is the same in pain and pleasure, rests in the self, regards a clod of earth, a stone and gold as equal, is the same towards the pleasant and unpleasant, steady, and the same in blame and praise...
verses.note: Gold and stone as equal is a vivid test. It is not about money being worthless but about your peace not depending on it.

verses.sa:
मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः।
सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते॥
verses.tr:
mānāpamānayos tulyas tulyo mitrāri-pakṣhayoḥ
sarvārambha-parityāgī guṇātītaḥ sa uchyate
verses.en: The same in honour and dishonour, the same to friend and foe, having given up all self-driven undertakings: such a person is said to have risen above the gunas.
verses.note: Giving up self-driven undertakings means no longer starting things just to feed the ego. Work continues; the hidden motive changes.

15.title: The supreme self
15.summary: Krishna describes the world as an upside-down ashvattha tree, its roots above and branches below, and teaches how to cut it with detachment. Each living being is a fragment of the eternal, and the divine dwells in every heart.
15.reflect: What would 'cutting the tree with detachment' (15.1 to 15.3) mean for one attachment you carry?

verses.sa:
श्री भगवानुवाच
ऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम्।
छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित्॥
verses.tr:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
ūrdhva-mūlam adhaḥ-śhākham aśhvatthaṁ prāhur avyayam
chhandānsi yasya parṇāni yas taṁ veda sa veda-vit
verses.en: The Lord said: They speak of an imperishable ashvattha tree with roots above and branches below. Its leaves are the Vedic hymns. One who knows it knows the Vedas.
verses.note: The inverted tree is a map of existence: its source is above in the infinite, its branches spread below into the world. Understanding the structure of the tree is understanding everything.

verses.sa:
ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः।
मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति॥
verses.tr:
mamaivānśho jīva-loke jīva-bhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ
manaḥ-ṣhaṣhṭhānīndriyāṇi prakṛiti-sthāni karṣhati
verses.en: An eternal fragment of myself has become the living soul in the world of beings. It draws to itself the senses, with the mind as the sixth, which rest in nature.
verses.note: Every being carries a fragment of the eternal. It gives each person intrinsic dignity, whatever their role.

verses.sa:
सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च।
वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम्॥
verses.tr:
sarvasya chāhaṁ hṛidi sanniviṣhṭo
mattaḥ smṛitir jñānam apohanaṁ cha
vedaiśh cha sarvair aham eva vedyo
vedānta-kṛid veda-vid eva chāham
verses.en: I am seated in the hearts of all. From me come memory, knowledge and their loss. I am what is to be known through all the Vedas; I am the author of Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas.
verses.note: The divine as the source of memory and knowledge, and of forgetting too. All learning, in this view, is ultimately coming to know what is already within.

16.title: Divine and demonic qualities
16.summary: Krishna contrasts two kinds of nature. The divine qualities lead to freedom; the demonic ones (arrogance, cruelty, endless craving) lead to bondage. Three gates lead to self-destruction: desire, anger and greed.
16.reflect: Which of the three gates in 16.21 is most often open for you, and what closes it?

verses.sa:
श्री भगवानुवाच
अभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिः ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः।
दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम्॥
verses.tr:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
abhayaṁ sattva-sanśhuddhir jñāna-yoga-vyavasthitiḥ
dānaṁ damaśh cha yajñaśh cha svādhyāyas tapa ārjavam
verses.en: The Lord said: Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfastness in knowledge and yoga, generosity, self-control, sacrifice, study of scripture, discipline and straightforwardness...
verses.note: The list of divine qualities opens with fearlessness. It comes first because fear distorts every other virtue.

verses.sa:
अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम्।
दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम्॥
verses.tr:
ahinsā satyam akrodhas tyāgaḥ śhāntir apaiśhunam
dayā bhūteṣhv aloluptvaṁ mārdavaṁ hrīr achāpalam
verses.en: Non-violence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, renunciation, peace, not finding fault, compassion for beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty and steadiness...
verses.note: Not finding fault (apaishunam) sits among the great virtues. Constant criticism of others is a habit that hardens the heart.

verses.sa:
तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता।
भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत॥
verses.tr:
tejaḥ kṣhamā dhṛitiḥ śhaucham adroho nāti-mānitā
bhavanti sampadaṁ daivīm abhijātasya bhārata
verses.en: Vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, cleanliness, freedom from malice and from excessive pride: these belong to one born with the divine nature, Arjuna.
verses.note: Vigour and fortitude are virtues too. The divine nature is not passive; it is energetic, resilient and forgiving at once.

verses.sa:
त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः।
कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत्॥
verses.tr:
tri-vidhaṁ narakasyedaṁ dvāraṁ nāśhanam ātmanaḥ
kāmaḥ krodhas tathā lobhas tasmād etat trayaṁ tyajet
verses.en: Desire, anger and greed: these are the three gates to hell that destroy the self. Therefore give up these three.
verses.note: A compact diagnosis. Most personal and organisational disasters can be traced to one of these three gates.

17.title: The three kinds of faith
17.summary: Arjuna asks about those who act with faith but outside scripture. Krishna explains that faith takes the shape of a person's nature and shows how food, sacrifice, discipline and giving each come in sattvic, rajasic and tamasic forms.
17.reflect: What does your faith, the thing you most deeply trust, say about who you are?

verses.sa:
सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत।
श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः॥
verses.tr:
sattvānurūpā sarvasya śhraddhā bhavati bhārata
śhraddhā-mayo ‘yaṁ puruṣho yo yach-chhraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ
verses.en: Everyone's faith matches their nature, Arjuna. A person is made of their faith: whatever their faith is, that is what they are.
verses.note: Shraddhamayo'yam purushah: a person is made of faith. What you deeply trust shapes who you become. Choosing what to trust is choosing who to be.

verses.sa:
अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत्।
स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते॥
verses.tr:
anudvega-karaṁ vākyaṁ satyaṁ priya-hitaṁ cha yat
svādhyāyābhyasanaṁ chaiva vāṅ-mayaṁ tapa uchyate
verses.en: Words that cause no distress, that are truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular study of scripture: this is called the discipline of speech.
verses.note: A four-part test for speech: does it avoid needless hurt, is it true, is it kind, does it help? A practical rule for feedback and meetings.

verses.sa:
दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे।
देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम्॥
verses.tr:
dātavyam iti yad dānaṁ dīyate ‘nupakāriṇe
deśhe kāle cha pātre cha tad dānaṁ sāttvikaṁ smṛitam
verses.en: A gift given because it is right to give, to someone who cannot repay it, at the right place and time, to a worthy person, is called sattvic.
verses.note: Pure giving expects nothing back, and is also wise about place, time and recipient. Generosity and judgement go together.

18.title: Liberation through renunciation
18.summary: The final chapter gathers the whole teaching: true renunciation is giving up the fruits of action, not action itself. Krishna returns to svadharma, gives his most secret teaching of surrender, and then leaves Arjuna free to decide. Arjuna rises, his confusion gone.
18.reflect: Krishna ends with 'reflect fully, then do as you wish.' After 18 Sundays, what do you now choose?

verses.sa:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्।
स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्॥
verses.tr:
śhreyān swa-dharmo viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt sv-anuṣhṭhitāt
svabhāva-niyataṁ karma kurvan nāpnoti kilbiṣham
verses.en: Better your own duty done imperfectly than another's duty done well. One who does the work suited to their own nature incurs no fault.
verses.note: The Gita returns to 3.35 at its close: your path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one done well. It is a final word on authenticity.

verses.sa:
सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत्।
सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः॥
verses.tr:
saha-jaṁ karma kaunteya sa-doṣham api na tyajet
sarvārambhā hi doṣheṇa dhūmenāgnir ivāvṛitāḥ
verses.en: Do not abandon the work you were born to, Arjuna, even if it has flaws. Every undertaking is covered by some fault, as fire is covered by smoke.
verses.note: No work is flawless; every fire has smoke. Waiting for a perfect path is a way of never walking one.

verses.sa:
इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया।
विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु॥
verses.tr:
iti te jñānam ākhyātaṁ guhyād guhyataraṁ mayā
vimṛiśhyaitad aśheṣheṇa yathechchhasi tathā kuru
verses.en: Thus I have taught you knowledge more secret than all secrets. Reflect on it fully, and then do as you wish.
verses.note: Perhaps the Gita's most remarkable verse. After all the teaching, Krishna does not command; he asks Arjuna to think it through and choose freely. A model for every mentor.

verses.sa:
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज।
अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः॥
verses.tr:
sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṁ śharaṇaṁ vraja
ahaṁ tvāṁ sarva-pāpebhyo mokṣhayiṣhyāmi mā śhuchaḥ
verses.en: Abandon all forms of dharma and simply surrender to me alone. I will free you from all sin; do not grieve.
verses.note: The final teaching: when rules and duties become confusing, surrender to the highest. Many read it as the call to drop the anxious calculation and trust.

verses.sa:
यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः।
तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम॥
verses.tr:
yatra yogeśhvaraḥ kṛiṣhṇo yatra pārtho dhanur-dharaḥ
tatra śhrīr vijayo bhūtir dhruvā nītir matir mama
verses.en: Wherever there is Krishna, the lord of yoga, and wherever there is Arjuna, the archer, there will surely be fortune, victory, prosperity and sound policy. That is my conviction.
verses.note: Sanjaya's closing words: wisdom and capable action together bring victory. Neither alone is enough; the guide and the doer must meet.
